meta.title: Inference service dataflow · Agentic inference · AI Data Center
meta.description: Seven-stage inference service dataflow: boot, idle start, model load, Question, Prefill, Decode, Answer. 8-way PD disaggregated: 4 Prefill + 4 Decode.

page.lead: The same inference server (CPU + DRAM + local SSD + 8× NPU/HBM, PD disaggregated: top row 4 Prefill cards, bottom row 4 Decode cards) is shown top-to-bottom across seven stages. CPU/DRAM hosts two Docker containers and two independent vLLM instances: Prefill binds to NPU 0–3 and Decode to NPU 4–7; model weights and KV Cache live in HBM. Gray means idle; color means active or on-disk artifacts.
page.summary: Seven stages: idle → boot (2× Docker / 2× vLLM into DRAM) → model load (SSD→DRAM→HBM) → Question → top Prefill (write KV) → bottom Decode (token by token) → Answer.

s0.title: Server not started
s0.summary: The machine is fully idle: CPU, DRAM, NPU, and HBM are not serving inference. Local SSD may already hold OS, drivers, Docker images, and model weights, but the service process is not up.
s0.l1: CPU idle. Inference engine, scheduler, and tokenizer are not running.
s0.l2: DRAM idle. No Docker process or request/token staging data in memory.
s0.l3: Files on SSD. OS, drivers, Docker image, and weights are mounted (blue), waiting to load after boot.
s0.l4: NPU / HBM idle. The 8-card pool is not computing yet.

s1.title: Server boot (model not loaded)
s1.summary: The inference service is up with two Docker containers and two independent vLLM instances in CPU + DRAM. Prefill is bound to NPU 0–3 and Decode to NPU 4–7. All 8 NPUs are powered, but HBM is still empty. No model weights yet.
s1.l1: Two instances ready. Docker #1 runs Prefill vLLM; Docker #2 runs Decode vLLM.
s1.l2: Explicit resource isolation. Prefill uses NPU 0–3 and Decode uses NPU 4–7; both runtimes remain resident in DRAM, not HBM.
s1.l3: Not inferencing. Weights remain on SSD; HBM has no weights and no Question is accepted yet.

s2.title: Load model (SSD → DRAM → HBM)
s2.summary: The loader reads model weights (safetensors) from SSD into DRAM buffer, then PyTorch/CUDA materializes weight tensors into each NPU’s HBM (PD disaggregated · per-card shards). HBM gains a weights region (~15%) and reserves KV Cache space.
s2.l1: Read disk. CPU/loader reads weights from SSD into DRAM (green highlight).
s2.l2: DRAM → HBM. Weight tensors are written to each NPU HBM via CUDA.
s2.l3: Ready. Weights stay resident in HBM (~15%); the server can accept requests.

s3.title: Question arrival (CPU side)
s3.summary: The user Question enters CPU over the network; the tokenizer on the DRAM side converts text to a token sequence and it is sent to NPU for Prefill. HBM already holds weights (~15%); KV compute has not started.
s3.l2: Tokenize. CPU converts text to token IDs in DRAM.
s3.l3: To NPU. The scheduler sends tokens to the NPU pool for Prefill.

s4.title: Prefill (read full Question, build KV Cache)
s4.summary: Input tokens move H2D into the top 4 Prefill cards’ HBM, process the full prompt using resident weights, fill the KV region, and emit the first Answer token (TTFT); bottom Decode cards wait.
s4.l1: Dispatch. Token sequence moves from DRAM into NPU HBM.
s4.l2: Prefill compute. NPU cores run CUDA kernels, reuse HBM weights, and create KV Cache.
s4.l3: First token. First output token arrives; TTFT ends.

s5.title: Decode (generate Answer token by token)
s5.summary: Each Decode step reuses HBM weights and KV Cache, appends new K/V, and samples one token until EOS. PD disaggregated · top Prefill / bottom Decode roles.
s5.l1: Read KV. NPU reads KV Cache and the previous token from HBM.
s5.l2: Decode step. Reuse weights, append K/V, sample one token.

s6.title: Answer return (CPU side)
s6.summary: The full token sequence returns from NPU HBM to DRAM; CPU detokenizes to Answer text on the DRAM side and sends it back over the network.
s6.l1: Write back. Token sequence lands in DRAM.
s6.l3: Deliver. Return to the user over the network.
